biography.plain_text: Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan was a French-born prince and international civil servant from the Aga Khan dynasty. The son of Aga Khan III, he became the youngest United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees and led the agency through crises across Asia and Africa. He later founded the Bellerive Foundation for environmental protection.

long_biography.plain_text:
Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan led the United Nations refugee agency through a decisive shift beyond Europe as its youngest and longest-serving High Commissioner. He strengthened cooperation with African governments and improved coordination across the United Nations. His tenure encompassed the Bangladesh refugee crisis, displacement from Burundi and the expulsion of South Asians from Uganda.

His interest in Islamic art produced a collection assembled throughout his life with Princess Catherine. Paintings, manuscripts and ceramics from their Château de Bellerive now form the core of the Aga Khan Museum's holdings. The museum recreates their Persian Salon in its Bellerive Room, preserving the collection's original domestic setting.
long_biography.html:
Prince Sadruddin Aga Khan led the United Nations refugee agency through a decisive shift beyond Europe as its youngest and longest-serving High Commissioner. He strengthened cooperation with African governments and improved coordination across the United Nations. His tenure encompassed the Bangladesh refugee crisis, displacement from Burundi and the expulsion of South Asians from Uganda.

His interest in Islamic art produced a collection assembled throughout his life with Princess Catherine. Paintings, manuscripts and ceramics from their Château de Bellerive now form the core of the Aga Khan Museum's holdings. The museum recreates their Persian Salon in its Bellerive Room, preserving the collection's original domestic setting.
